subject: Order Form redlines: indemnity, takedown SLA, evidence bundle
messages:
From: Emily Rhodes <emily.rhodes@novapulse.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>; Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Novapulse Procurement <procurement@novapulse.com>
Date: 2025-08-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: MSA redlines + takedown SLA question

Hi Olga / Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move ahead. Procurement attached our redline of the MSA and the order form (see Novapulse_MSA_redline_2025.docx). A couple of items legal flagged as blockers for our security team:

- Indemnity carveouts: customer requests explicit defense for 3P IP claims and a narrower customer notice window (24 hrs).
- Takedown / emergency removal: their counsel wants the right to request immediate removal of specific generated content without requiring a court order (they see this as an operational safety requirement).
- Evidence obligations: they requested a detailed evidence list and a requirement for Redwood to preserve or export model logs/KV cache on request.

Can you confirm whether these are acceptable, or propose alternate language? We can do a legal call if that helps.

Emily
Emily Rhodes
Senior Counsel, Novapulse
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Date: 2025-08-12T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: MSA redlines + takedown SLA question

Folks — forwarding Novapulse redlines. Key asks that I want legal and commercial input on before we respond:

1) 24-hour notice for IP claims + unilateral takedown rights for customer (they want immediate removal if content "poses risk").
2) Evidence preservation: they want us to export logs, KV cache, and training prompt history on a per-claim basis and hold data for 3 years.
3) Scope of indemnity: they propose we accept defense for third-party infringement broadly but carve out model-generated content where customer provided the prompt.

Ben: this is at a stage where procurement is sensitive to turnaround time; they asked for a response by EOD Thursday. Can you own the commercial reply if legal provides language?

Kimberly / Jonas: any redline language you prefer? I'm worried about the operational burden of ad-hoc KV cache exports and the risk of exposing internal telemetry.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Sr. Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Novapulse_MSA_redline_2025.docx, evidence_capture_template.xlsx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-12T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines + takedown SLA question

Thanks for the heads up. High-level legal position and suggested fallback language below — keeping it pragmatic so sales can keep the deal momentum.

Quick positions:
- 24-hr notice: unacceptable as a hard requirement for all claims. We can agree to a short preliminary notice window for content-removal requests, but we must keep an explicit cure period for IP claims (30 days) except for emergency takedowns tied to imminent harm.
- Customer unilateral takedown: we will not accept a broad unilateral takedown right without a court order or express regulatory trigger. We can accept an operational "emergency takedown" clause limited to specific enumerated scenarios (e.g., direct threat to safety, illegal content) with review rights.
- Evidence export: we can provide a scoped evidence package (logs, request/response transcript, hashed KV snapshots) on a per-claim basis subject to mutual confidentiality and standard discovery process. We should avoid committing to full raw KV cache export or indefinite retention.
- Indemnity scope: counterproposal is to accept defense & indemnity for third-party IP claims alleging infringement arising from the model output, PROVIDED customer used the service in compliance with the order form and gave reasonable notice. We will carve out claims where customer knowingly uploaded infringing data or used the model to reproduce third-party content from a dataset they provided.

Suggested redline text (short form):
"Redwood shall defend and indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the Model Output, when used in accordance with the Agreement, infringes a third party's intellectual property rights; provided (i) Customer provides prompt written notice, (ii) Redwood has sole control of the defense, and (iii) Customer cooperates in the defense. For clarity, Redwood's obligations shall not apply to claims arising from Customer-provided data or instructions that cause the Model Output to reproduce a Customer-supplied third-party work."

Operational asks for ENG / Ops: we need a standard evidence bundle template (minimal required items) and an engineering SLA for producing it (e.g., 5 business days for hashed logs and transcript export; 15 business days for additional telemetry) — but these are commercial asks to balance the risk.

I'll prepare a marked-up MSA with the above language; Ben can lead on procurement timing and the mutual action plan.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Emily Rhodes <emily.rhodes@novapulse.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-13T08:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines: indemnity, takedown SLA, evidence bundle

Emily / Novapulse — thanks for sending. Appreciate the urgency. To be transparent, Redwood wants to keep response timing tight but also avoid operational open-ended commitments. Proposed path:

1) Compromise on notice: customer provides a "Preliminary Notice" (within 48 hours) for content remediation/takedown requests; for IP claims we request a 30-day cure period except in enumerated emergency scenarios.
2) Evidence bundle: Redwood will provide a standard package within 5 business days (request/response transcript, request metadata, content hash, and a redacted KV snapshot). If more forensic output is requested, that will be provided under an executed mutual NDA + reasonable cost recovery for engineering time.
3) Indemnity redline: Accept in principle with the carveouts Kimberly noted. We'll attach an appendix (evidence_capture_template.xlsx) that lists the standard items we'll provide and the expected SLA.

Ben — I'll sync with you on the mutual action plan. Would you propose times for a 30-minute legal-to-legal call tomorrow?

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Order Form redlines: indemnity, takedown SLA, evidence bundle

Emily — quick note to lock the next steps so we don't lose momentum:

- We agree to a short legal sync (30 minutes) to go through the revised redline language and evidence appendix. Proposed times: 2025-08-15 09:00 PT or 2025-08-15 13:00 PT — which works for you?
- We'll upload a marked MSA with Kimberly's suggested language and the evidence appendix to the Drive link (shared after this email).
- For operational clarity, Redwood will commit to the standard evidence package within 5 business days and make an engineering estimate (and any pass-through cost) for additional exports.
- If Novapulse is comfortable after the call, we can proceed with a conditional DocuSign routing for the order form while legal works through final MSA items.

Emily (Procurement) — can you confirm the earliest acceptable SLA for the evidence package and whether Novapulse is willing to sign an SLA appendix that limits expedited exports to defined emergencies?

Thanks — will stand by for time confirmation.

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
